classificationDefinitions.ENFORCED: an executable artefact proves it (test, verifier script, migration, policy or machine-checked contract match) and, where a boundary is declared, a real call site invokes it
classificationDefinitions.DECLARED: a module, document or contract mentions it, but nothing executable proves it
classificationDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED: implementation and tests exist, but the declared boundary patterns match nothing — the capability protects nothing yet

ownership.note: Phase 19 owns alert definitions/state, incident records/lifecycle and the operational composition contract. It does not own canonical state, design language or the human interface layer.

areas.area: Health state is scoped, fresh and never fabricated
areas.requirement: Unknown or stale state is not healthy, command context is complete and cross-tenant command access requires an explicit grant.

areas.area: Alerts preserve source, priority, escalation and flood control
areas.requirement: Alerts require source provenance, carry explainable priority, escalate only under policy, correlate related alerts and suppress floods.

areas.area: Incidents and decisions require ordered, attributable handling
areas.requirement: Incidents transition legally, retain commanders/responders/evidence and postmortems, while decisions have owners, approval, expiry and a minimum option set.

areas.area: Operational read models are ordered, fresh and audited
areas.requirement: Events preserve sequence and correlation, duplicate delivery is rejected, caches expire or invalidate, sensitive views are authorized and high-impact actions receive enhanced audit treatment.

areas.area: Unknown actions, break-glass and recovery remain controlled
areas.requirement: Unverified actions are never displayed as success, rollback is offered only for failed or unknown states, break-glass access is justified and time-boxed, and degraded mode is read-only.

areas.area: Operational engines are not yet projected by the visible surface
areas.requirement: A real operational surface must consume command health, alert and incident state; the existing governance-surface tests do not prove that the visible Command Centre renders these engines.

limitations: Classification measures the presence of executable evidence, not the correctness or completeness of that evidence.
A DECLARED area is unfinished work, never a false claim — it is reported as such.
An IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED area has a tested implementation that no boundary calls; it is reported, never counted as enforcement.
Evidence patterns are declared per phase in architecture/phase-acceptance/phase-<id>-*.json and must be reviewed when a phase is re-audited.
